page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs running on a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no local storage and no dedicated graphics accelerators, relying exclusively on network-attached storage solutions, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate a split performance profile driven by the instance topology. Single-threaded execution ranks in the upper quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1990.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 3071.58. Conversely, multithreaded capacity ranks in the bottom 25%, constrained by the two-thread limit across one physical core; Geekbench multi-core achieved 2473.0, and the PassMark CPU score registered at 3810.31. Large-block memory write bandwidth sits in the middle 50% at 27.48 GB/sec, whereas read-only large-block memory throughput reaches 36.94 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also rank in lower tiers.

Regarding hardware efficiency, the server delivers high per-thread compute capability paired with substantial memory density. Because local storage is absent, storage input/output relies entirely on network interfaces, which can constrain disk-heavy tasks. The instance serves environments requiring larger RAM buffers per thread without necessitating heavy multi-core parallelism, such as lightweight in-memory caching tiers, memory-bound background tasks, small transactional database replicas, and low-traffic web microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core running at 2.7 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive operations. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage disks, necessitating remote network-attached volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Architectural benchmarks reflect strong single-core performance alongside modest multi-core capacity, consistent with its dual-thread hardware layout. Large-block memory write bandwidth operates within median ranges, while database operations exhibit lower aggregate throughput. This hardware profile functions effectively for workloads requiring modest compute capacity coupled with significant memory allocations, such as small in-memory caches, lightweight database read replicas, and low-scale web applications.
